subject: Post-demo: Vectorly embedding transition & arch next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liao <sara@vectorly.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vectorly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Vectorly embedding transition & arch next steps

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great session, and super helpful to see your re-ranker flows and how you currently store vectors. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum.

Summary of what you shared:
- Current embeddings provider: Embeddify (v2) with 1536-d vectors, index in Elasticsearch with L2 normalization turned off.
- Typical request pattern: high-QPS search traffic during business hours (burst to ~500 qps), many small queries (avg query tokens < 64).
- Pipeline: user query -> embedding -> ANN index -> reranker (server-side).

Redwood integration focus areas we discussed:
- SDK setup & auth: language SDK + token routing per environment (staging/prod), short-lived tokens via your existing Vault/KMS.
- Routing: warm path to dedicated capacity during peak, fallback to hosted models for spikes.
- Structured output/tool-calling: not needed for this initial migration but will plan hooks for future reranker calls.
- Embeddings specifics: target vector dim support (1536), batch sizing recommendations, prefix/KV cache considerations, and recommended normalization strategy (we suggested L2 normalize on ingest).

Immediate next steps I propose (action owners in parens):
1) Vector export sample and schema from your side — one weekly index segment (10k vectors) and one recent user query (Tom) (Vectorly)
2) Redwood will provide a quick-run conversion script + sample SDK snippet for migrating Embeddify vectors to Redwood-compatible format (Marissa/Ben)
3) Architecture note from Karthik on optimal batch sizes, normalization, and route policies for your traffic profile (Karthik)
4) Security checklist and SOC2-driven evidence we discussed (Redwood to attach)

I attached a short transition checklist and a couple of SDK snippets to start. Can you confirm Tom or someone on your infra team can share a small export by EOD Monday (Nov 2)? If that timeline is tight, tell us what works and we’ll adapt.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Vectorly embedding transition & arch next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. Quick clarifications from our side: we can export a sample (10k vectors) and a few hours of query logs by EOD Monday. A couple of technical points to flag up front:

- Dimensionality: yes, our current Embeddify vectors are fixed at 1536. We're open to quantization on ingest but need to understand latency tradeoffs.
- Normalization: we currently index raw vectors (no L2) and apply cosine similarity by normalizing in query. If Redwood prefers L2-normalized vectors at ingest that is OK but we want guidance on cost/space impact.
- Batching: our producer can send batches of 256 vectors max; we can adjust to 128 if that helps throughput.
- Auth: we use HashiCorp Vault for secrets; we can grant a short-term read token for the export.

One ask: can Redwood share an approximate tokenized cost estimate for storage/queries when moving from Embeddify to your platform (ballpark per million queries)? If you don’t have exact numbers now, a conservative estimate is fine to help our finance review.

On timing — Tom will upload the export to the drive link you provided. Thanks.

—Tom
Senior Platform Engineer | Vectorly Inc
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liao <sara@vectorly.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vectorly.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: Vectorly embedding transition & arch next steps

Looping in a quick architecture note — high level guidance based on the profile Tom shared. Will refine after we see the sample export.

Recommendations:
- Vector dim: Redwood runtime supports 1536 natively; keep dims unchanged for initial cutover. If you later quantize to int8/4-bit, we can show perf/cost tradeoffs.
- Normalization: L2-normalize on ingest is recommended for consistent ANN behavior and smaller index variance. If you currently normalize on query, moving to ingest normalization reduces per-query CPU. Impact: ~3-5% index size increase for float32 vectors (but can be mitigated by post-quantization).
- Batching: aim for producer-side batches of 128 for optimal CPU/GPU throughput in Redwood Dedicated; we recommend a batching window of 50-150 ms to balance latency and throughput.
- Migration flow: ingest pipeline = export -> redwood-convert (small ETL we’ll provide) -> ingest into staging index -> run backfill re-ranks against a sample traffic replay (we can assist with a sandbox replay).
- Routing: create a canary route to Dedicated for 5% traffic, auto-roll to 100% if latency/SLA targets met over 24h. Configure fallback to hosted model variant on overload.
- SDK/Auth: use our short-lived token flow with Vault integration; we’ll provide Terraform snippet to automate token issuance and rotation.

Actionable asks from us to Vectorly:
1) Export sample + query logs (Tom)
2) Grant read-only Vault token for one-time export (Ops)
3) Confirm target SLOs for latency and p95 tail (business)

I’ll draft a minimal ETL script tonight and attach to the drive link.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

If anything shifts on your side please flag ASAP. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the above plan.

Best —
